name: Workshop | A Preamble of Our Own with Kriti Monga
description: A creative, hands-on (typography + embroidery)  workshop with designer-artist Kriti Monga, to understand, reflect and engage with our Preamble and the  values it outlines. We've created a custom typographic design of the Indian Preamble, and you're invited to embroider and make it your own! Join us, as we collectively reflect on the values of the Preamble, learn basic embroidery and spend the morning stitching together. Here are the details: Date:  28 November 2026, Saturday Time:   10:00 AM - 1:00 PM Venue :  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanthnagar Workshop fee:   INR 3000   Limited seats.  Register your spot. Who is it for:  Open to all above age 12 What is included in the fee:  1 custom designed pre-printed t-shirt or tote bag or frameable fabric + various coloured threads and needles for stitching your piece + light snacks.     About the facilitator: Kriti Monga brings 22 years of an accomplished design career to her multi-disciplinary creative practice that lies at the intersection of strategic design, artistic expression and hands-on craftsmanship. Founder-Director of Turmeric Design, her oeuvre spans brand building, book design, visual art, illustration and creative mentorship.  Trained at the National Institute of Design and Barcelona Academy of Art, she teaches professional programmes in design and typography around the world.   Embroidery instruction: Embroidery instruction by Suhani Chheda, a textile design graduate from NID, working at the intersection of impact, sustainability and textiles. Suhani's practice is rooted in Indian history, culture, and aesthetics, and involves experimenting across material and textile mediums. She is currently a part of the founding team building India's first post-consumer textile waste ecosystem.   Limited seats.  Register your spot.

name: Book Discussion | 'We, the People of India: Decoding a Nation’s Symbols' by T.M. Krishna with #ReclaimConstitution
description: What defines a nation? Is it the flag, the anthem, the emblem, or the Constitution that binds us together? Join us for a special weekend celebrating the Constitution through music, history, archival recordings and the stories behind our national symbols.  Using T.M. Krishna’s book  We, The People of India ,  Vinay Kumar  from  #ReclaimConstitution  will explore how these symbols acquired their meanings, how those meanings have been contested, and what they reveal about our identity and sense of belonging. Join us on a journey to look beyond the familiar and discover why these symbols deserve a closer reading. This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. There will also be a curated book shelf along with a replica of the hand calligraphed first edition of the Constitution on display at the bookstore with an opportunity to go home with a hand printed Preamble as well. Here are the details: Date:  28 November 2026, Saturday Time:  6:00 PM  Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanthnagar RSVP here to register. About the book: India’s independence came at the cost of millions of lives and deep psychological scars. As attempts were made to urgently stitch together the states and princely provinces that would eventually comprise the Republic of India, members of the Constituent Assembly and the newly formed government also debated the symbols—the national flag, anthem, emblem, motto and Preamble—that could represent the free people of the new nation and reinforce in them a sense of their own identity as citizens.  Not all of the processes and communications around this passage from idea to symbol were clearly documented. It is this lack of ready historical material that set musician and cultural commentator T.M. Krishna on a journey of discovery that shaped itself into this extraordinary book. Through meticulous research and persistent questioning, he found ways to explore the historical, cultural and philosophical contexts of each symbol, revealing how they evolved to become powerful metaphors for a nation’s aspirations, struggles and dreams for the future. In tracing the origin and evolution of the tricolour with the chakra in the centre, the discussions about the significance of the lions on the Ashokan pillar capitals and the proclamations to be included in the Preamble to the Constitution of India, the debates around the adoption of the motto ‘Satyameva Jayate’ and Tagore’s Jana Gana Mana, leading up to the present controversy around Vande Mataram, Krishna invites readers to reconsider the significance of each of these symbols in contemporary India. Written with a deep sincerity and analytical clarity,  We, the People of India  is an eloquent meditation on constitutionalism, freedom and the importance of effective representation in a complex, vibrant democracy. It is also, ultimately, a citizenly response to a nation in crisis. About the moderator: Vinay Kumar  is an aerospace engineer and the founder of #ReclaimConstitution, a national initiative working to build a constitutional culture among young people. Through innovative workshops, public programmes and the #ReclaimConstitution Quiz, he brings the Constitution out of textbooks, into everyday conversations. Vinay combines his background in research with a deep interest in education to enhance public understanding of the Constitution. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Spirit of Inquiry: The Constitution Day Quiz
description: This Constitution Day, join us, along with #ReclaimConstitution and QShala, for an evening of questions, stories and discoveries about India’s Constitution. Explore the people, ideas and unexpected connections behind the document that shapes our everyday lives—and win special prizes and Constitution memorabilia and goodies.  Here are the details: Date:  26 November 2026, Thursday Time:  7:00 PM  Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Indiranagar Participation fee:  INR 250 ( of which Rs 100 is redeemable against books and valid for up to a year) RSVP here to register. Who is it for? An open-to-all quiz for curious minds. No prior knowledge of law required. About the quizmaster: Raghav Chakravarthy  is a lawyer turned quizmaster and co-founder of QShala, a quiz and curiosity-based learning platform working with children, families, schools and institutions across India. Over the past decade, QShala has engaged more than 250 schools and built one of South Asia’s largest family quiz communities. A National Tata Crucible Champion (2012), Raghav has designed and hosted over 500 quizzes across school, college, family and corporate formats. He has served as quizmaster for Conquest, one of India’s longest-running college quizzes on the Indian Constitution, and helmed AmiQuiz Curiae, an all-India quiz for lawyers.  He is also the author of  Ready for the Law Challenge , published by Juggernaut. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Book discussion | 'A Sort of Homecoming': Indian fiction writing in 2026
description: What’s Indian fiction writing in 2026 like? Between evolving readership, self-publishing platforms, AI writing and translations, how has an author’s journey changed? Join us for a retrospective with  The Deodar Prize  authors as they talk about their experiences and unveil the best stories of 2026, with  Aadit Basu , the 2026 winner and  Sumanya Velamur , shortlisted in 2024 in conversation with  Ratul Ghosh , the runner-up for The Deodar Prize in 2023. This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:   21 November 2026, Saturday Time:  6:00 PM  Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanthnagar RSVP here to register. About the book: Tigers can be pets. The government can snatch your home. A midlife crisis can land you, fully clothed, in a swimming pool. From a vengeful goddess to a vomiting rice cooker, these stories carefully tread the ordinary alongside the fantastic. Short stories, like dreams, are visceral, vivid and hard to reconstruct; yet each bite leaves a distinct flavour on the tongue. Sweet. Sour. Salty. Spicy. Umami. Pick your flavour. About the speakers:  Sumanya Anand Velamur   is a researcher, social worker, impact consultant, and writer. She is based in Bengaluru. Her fiction and non-fiction works have been published in  Kitaab, Feminism in India, Mean Pepper Vine, USAWA, Out of Print Blog, Quibble Lit,  and  Quillmark . Her stories were longlisted for the Hope Prize, 2025 and shortlisted for the Deodar Prize (and featured in the Deodar 2024 anthology), 2024 and the BWW R.K.Anand Prize, 2024.  Aadit Basu   is a writer and designer based in Bangalore. By day, he is the founder of morphous Design Lab, a studio working at the intersection of craft and technology, solving problems that no one knew they had. He started his career as an architectural photographer, then became an artist investigating contemporary culture, but writing has always been at the heart of it all. He writes across fiction, poetry and cultural criticism, often drawn to memory, the internet and the strange absurdities of urban life. About the moderator: Till he had to care for his father,  Ratul Ghosh   was a conventional engineer-MBA-CXO. As part of the reset, he started writing fiction about suffering and caring. He was runners-up at the inaugural Deodar Prize and was awarded the BWW RK Anand Memorial Award last year. His publications include  Hammock, Usawa, Bangalore Review, Out of Print, Muse India  and  Hooghly Review . He lives in Bangalore and is currently writing a memoir and a collection of short fiction. name: Book Launch | ‘Mahua Matters’: Stories, Memory and Flavour
description: Mahua is more than a flower. Rooted in forest ecologies, community knowledge, food cultures and livelihoods, it carries stories that are often overlooked.  Mahua Matters , a publication by Wild Harvest India and Edible Issues and  Issue 1  brings together these stories through research, writing and flavour exploration.  Join us for a conversation with editors and the  Mahua Matters  team,  Shivani Unakar  and  Elizabeth Yorke , contributor  Kumud Dadlani , and chef  Hanna Sarangan  on the people and places behind the book, followed by a guided tasting that explores mahua’s many flavours and possibilities. Together, we’ll discover what it means to look at this flower in new ways and why its stories matter. This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:   22 November 2026, Sunday Time:   6:00 PM  Venue:   Champaca Bookstore, Vasanthnagar RSVP here to register. About the book: Mahua Matters   is a collaborative storytelling and engagement project by Wild Harvest and Edible Issues, dedicated to reintroducing and reimagining Mahua – a culturally significant, climate-resilient tree native to central and eastern India. For generations, Mahua flowers, seeds, and oil have been integral to the food, livelihoods, and traditions of many Adivasi and forest-dwelling communities. Yet, outside these communities, Mahua is often misunderstood, reduced to its association with country liquor, and overlooked for its rich cultural, ecological, and culinary value. Mahua Matters ,  Issue #1  brings together essays, research, speculative fiction, and recipes. From forest ecologies and Indigenous foodways, to history and policy, markets and contemporary kitchens, this book acts as a tangible starting point to exploring the multiplicity of mahua in India. This issue includes a new moveable Mahua Flavour Wheel—developed over a year of participatory Mahua Flavour Labs and public tastings—for readers to explore this ingredient in their own kitchens. About the speakers:  Elizabeth Yorke   is a food systems strategist, entrepreneur and researcher working at the intersection of food, sustainability, culture and innovation. A chef by training, her work explores how food can be a lens for understanding ecological, social and economic change. She is the co-creator of Edible Issues and founder of Saving Grains, and works across research, creative programmes, ventures and collaborations to imagine more resilient and regenerative food futures. Hanna Sarangan   is a Goa-based chef, business owner, and food consultant. With over a decade working in different parts of the world, her passion lies in creating ingredient-driven menus that celebrate foraged local and seasonal ingredients. For the last year, she's been working with Wild Harvest to develop mahua-based recipes, and familiarize consumers with creative ways to bring mahua into their kitchens. Kumud Dadlani   is a food culture strategist and storyteller who believes that eating is a political act. Her work wanders through farms, kitchens, and dining tables, exploring indigenous ingredients, ethical sourcing, and the power of food traditions. A graduate of the University of Gastronomic Sciences in Italy, she has worked with Slow Food International, Diaspora Co., and Impresario Hospitality, and her writing has appeared in Condé Nast Traveller India, The Hindu, and beyond. About the moderator: Shivani Unakar  is a Bangalore-based food culture researcher, exploring the intersection of food, people, and place. Through immersive fieldwork and public engagement, she translates complex food narratives into strategic storytelling and cultural programming for institutions, brands, and community projects.
